records.note: Description of a study in progress at Acacia Clinics, where the forecaster is a clinician and trial site ('along with colleagues from Acacia Clinics'). The study and the aim 'to make this available at scale' are own-organization actions. The sentence is also present-tense information with no outcome asserted. Own-organization trial; not scored.

'It will no longer be the status quo' names no observable event, benchmark, series or threshold for the PBM rebate and formulary-tiering practice. 'As soon as this law kicks into force in 2028' is a presupposition about a law signed the night before (its effective date is set by the enacted text, so that part would be KNOWN), not the claim. No event can be written without inventing a metric.

Assessment that CA 2026 'completely destroyed the financial rationale for PBMs as a profit center'. The implied future (the PBM units of Cigna, UnitedHealth and CVS stop being profit centers) has no metric, threshold, series or date in the words. Past-tense judgment; nothing observable can be written.

Retrospective remark about today's share price ('did not drop a stone today'). No future state is asserted, and the author hedges ('Either I'm missing something, or everybody else is'). An implied fall in UnitedHealth Group shares has no threshold or date.
'Is catastrophic' characterizes the 100 percent rebate pass-through requirement. The implied outcome (the PBM business model ends) names no observable event, threshold, series or date.
RICO analogy and slogan ('the kind of transparency that no racket can withstand'). The implied end of the PBM 'racket' has no entity-level event, benchmark or date.

'That's all over with' asserts that category-level opaque PBM reporting ends under CA 2026. Read as a legal fact it restates the signed law (KNOWN); read as a prediction about practice it has no series, threshold or date. No event can be written.

Compound hedge: (a) 'the status quo is gonna fight to preserve itself' and (b) 'I don't know if this is gonna actually change things'. Neither half names an observable event, actor decision, threshold or date. Both halves fail the same test, so one record.
'The worm has turned...maybe' is a metaphor about political sentiment toward PBMs. No body, action, benchmark or date can be written.

Restatement of Evernorth's own announcement that prior authorization for TMS ends for its contracted providers starting in March 2026. The deciding body had announced the outcome before the statement date. Not an expectation of the forecaster's own.

event.asset: Kale Award trial (bilateral versus unilateral TMS for suicidal ideation), as named by the author from Paul Fitzgerald's Brain Stimulation 2025 session
event.title: Kale Award trial reports its bilateral-versus-unilateral TMS result for suicidal ideation
event.proposition: The Kale Award trial reports its primary comparison of bilateral versus unilateral stimulation for suicidal ideation (either direction).
event.criterion: TRUE on the date of the first public report of the Kale Award trial's primary outcome result: the peer-reviewed primary results publication, the investigators' topline release, or a results posting in the trial's registry entry, whichever is first. The result may favour bilateral, unilateral or neither; the event is about a primary result being reported. A protocol publication, a recruitment update, an interim safety report or a conference abstract without the primary outcome estimate does not count. Resolution source: the peer-reviewed primary results publication (PubMed), with the trial registry entry as the secondary source.

resolution_source.name: Kale Award trial primary results publication (PubMed); trial registry entry as secondary source

readings: The trial is identified only by the author's words: 'the Kale Award trial', designed to test whether bilateral stimulation is superior to unilateral for suicidal ideation, discussed in Paul Fitzgerald's Brain Stimulation 2025 session. No registry number or sponsor is given, so none is written.
The claim is about timing, so the event resolves on the first public report of the primary outcome in either direction, not on which arm wins.

'It's years out from results' is read as a denial that a primary result is reported within the undated 24-month window from the statement date (2026-02-25 to 2028-02-25). A coder who reads the sentence as relayed session information would reject as REPORT or NOT_FORECAST.

records.stage_note: At the statement date the author describes the trial as existing ('There is now a named trial') with results years away. No base-rate class covers the timing of a trial readout, so abstain.
records.note: Flat declarative timing call: bin A on 'It's years out from results' (as earlier flat assertions such as 'That is soon'), asserts false, so p(result reported within the window) = 0.1. 'Years out' is not in the anchor table, so the item is undated and takes the 24-month window. The ClinicalTrials.gov table rule is not applied: the claim is about timing, not a result, and the author gives no registry entry. Not affiliated: no disclosed role in the trial (Acacia Clinics and Ampa are trial sites for other studies). Not a report: no source is cited for the timing.
Scientific claim about what will explain TMS outcome variance (coil angle versus coordinates). Not a regulatory, trial, company, payer or adoption outcome; 'ultimately' is also not a deadline.
'The more of those you file, the more you shift national coverage policy': quantifiers with no countable set, and no named payer, policy, threshold or date.
Commitment to keep writing about ERISA fiduciary duty in the forecaster's own newsletter. Own publication; not scored.
'This is how coverage standards change' restates owen-2101 as a general mechanism. No payer, policy, benchmark or date can be written.

Relays an announcement from the conference session ('announced in this session') that a worldwide non-invasive brain stimulation registry is being built. Passes on information; no expectation of the forecaster's own. A research registry is also outside the five areas.
